newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trade springs back to life.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trade springs back to life.

text.p: Trading on the Nigerian stock market roared back to life on Friday as more dealers returned from yuletide holidays.
The tempo of trading pushed the all-share index higher to 6999.95 from 6992.01 on Thursday.
Traders said more than two million shares changed hands at the session in which 45 dealers participated.

More equities were active again and price rises outnumbered losses. "Besides the gains in oil, food and banking sectors, insurance, agriculture, healthcare and construction stocks advanced," one trader said.
Texaco shares continued to excel on its improved half-year performance, closing 25 kobo up at 34.25 naira. African Petroleum also soared 20 kobo to 45.20 naira.

Among food companies, Nestle and Union Dicon Salt were 20 kobo ahead at 49.50 naira and 42.50 naira, respectively. Nigerian Bottling Company, still basking in the glow of a successful merger, ended 25 kobo stronger at 29.00 naira.
Union Bank was its sector's best performer, ending seven kobo up at 6.15 naira.

Okomu Oil Palm, the best performer on the exchange last year, added five kobo to close at 8.20 naira on Friday while construction firms Julius Berger and Cappa & D'Alberto rose by 10 kobo and four kobo, respectively to 8.80 naira and 7.40 naira.
Traders attributed the bull run to optimism that Nigeria's economy, now widely considered to have stabilised after a 1993 election crisis that paralysed Nigeria, would grow this year.
Some leading shares, however, closed down because of supply glut while lingering bad times accounted for others.
Nigerian Breweries fell five kobo to 19.25 naira, Dunlop dropped 12 kobo to 7.88 naira, Ashaka Cement lost five at 16.45 and Lever Brothers closed at 19.90 naira, down 10 kobo.
Chemical and allied Products drifted 30 kobo lower on its declining profitability. It closed at 5.70 naira.
Traders said caution would remain their watchword until the military rulers announce the 1997 budget in the next few weeks.
